questions.q: Which of the following is the SI unit of thermodynamic temperature?
questions.explanation: The kelvin (K) is the SI base unit of thermodynamic temperature.

questions.q: What is the unit of force in the CGS system?
questions.explanation: The dyne is the CGS unit of force (g cm s⁻²).

questions.q: How many dynes are there in one newton?
questions.explanation: 1 N = 1 kg m s⁻² = 1000 g × 100 cm s⁻² = 10⁵ dyne.

questions.q: How many significant figures does the number 100.50 have?
questions.explanation: Zeros between non-zero digits and trailing zeros after a decimal point are significant, so all 5 digits count.

questions.q: Which of the following has the same dimensions as angular velocity?
questions.explanation: Angular velocity (radian is dimensionless) has dimensions T⁻¹, the same as frequency.

questions.q: A quantity is calculated as X = a²b³/(c√d). The percentage errors in a, b, c and d are 1%, 2%, 3% and 4% respectively. What is the maximum percentage error in X?
A cuboid measures 2.0 cm × 3.00 cm × 4.0 cm. Report its volume with the correct number of significant figures.
keyPoints: In multiplication keep the least number of significant figures (2 here)
questions.explanation: The measurements 2.0 and 4.0 have two significant figures, which limits the result.

questions.q: Show that surface tension has the same dimensions as energy per unit area.
questions.explanation: This is why surface tension can also be expressed in J m⁻².

questions.q: Average velocity of a body over a time interval is defined as
questions.explanation: Average velocity = displacement divided by the time taken.

questions.q: The acceleration due to gravity near the Earth's surface is directed
options: downward, towards the centre of the Earth
in the direction of the object's motion
questions.explanation: Gravity always pulls towards the centre of the Earth, whatever the direction of motion.

questions.q: A ball is thrown vertically upward at 15 m s⁻¹. Taking g = 10 m s⁻², what is its velocity after 1 s?
questions.explanation: v = u − gt = 15 − 10 = 5 m s⁻¹, still upward.

questions.q: A body starts from rest with a uniform acceleration of 2 m s⁻². How far does it travel during the 3rd second alone?
questions.explanation: Distance in 3 s = ½ × 2 × 9 = 9 m; in 2 s = 4 m; so the 3rd second covers 5 m.

questions.q: A body starts from rest and moves with uniform acceleration. What is the ratio of the distance covered in the first 2 s to that covered in the first 4 s?
questions.explanation: s ∝ t², so the ratio is 2² : 4² = 1 : 4.

questions.q: Car B is 50 m behind car A on a straight road. A moves at 20 m s⁻¹ and B moves in the same direction at 25 m s⁻¹, both at constant speed. How long does B take to catch up with A?
questions.explanation: Relative speed = 5 m s⁻¹, so time = 50/5 = 10 s.

questions.q: A train travels at 60 km/h for 2 hours and then at 90 km/h for 1 hour. Find its average speed for the whole journey.
questions.explanation: Average speed is total distance divided by total time, not the mean of the two speeds.

questions.q: A ball moving upward passes a window at a speed of 10 m s⁻¹ (g = 10 m s⁻²). How much higher does it rise above the window, and how long after passing it does it return to the window?
questions.answer: It rises 5 m higher and returns after 2 s.
keyPoints: Return to the same level takes 2 × 1 = 2 s
questions.explanation: Up and down motions are symmetric about the highest point.

questions.q: The scalar (dot) product of two vectors is
questions.explanation: A · B = AB cosθ is a number with no direction.

questions.q: The vector product A × B is directed
options: perpendicular to the plane containing A and B
questions.explanation: By the right-hand rule, A × B is perpendicular to both A and B.

questions.q: What is the magnitude of the vector A = 6î − 8ĵ?
A particle moves in a circle with a time period of 0.5 s. What is its angular speed?
questions.explanation: ω = 2π/T = 2π/0.5 = 4π rad s⁻¹.

questions.q: A projectile is launched at 30 m s⁻¹ at 30° above the horizontal (g = 10 m s⁻²). After how long does it reach its highest point?
One car moves north at 10 m s⁻¹ and another moves east at 10 m s⁻¹. What is the speed of one relative to the other?
questions.explanation: The relative velocity is the vector difference of perpendicular velocities: √(10² + 10²) ≈ 14.1 m s⁻¹.

questions.q: A ball is thrown horizontally at 5 m s⁻¹. Taking g = 10 m s⁻², find its speed 1 s later.
keyPoints: Vertical velocity after 1 s = gt = 10 m s⁻¹
questions.explanation: Combine the unchanged horizontal component with the vertical component gained from gravity.

questions.q: A 0.5 kg stone is whirled in a horizontal circle of radius 1 m at a constant speed of 4 m s⁻¹ using a light string. Find the tension in the string.
questions.explanation: The only horizontal force on the stone is the tension, which must equal mv²/r.

questions.q: Newton's second law can be stated in terms of momentum p as
questions.explanation: The net force equals the rate of change of momentum.

questions.q: For the same pair of surfaces, which of the following is generally the largest?
questions.explanation: Limiting static friction is slightly larger than kinetic friction, and rolling friction is far smaller.

questions.q: Forces of 12 N and 6 N act on a 3 kg body in the same direction. What is the acceleration?
questions.explanation: Net force = 18 N, so a = 18/3 = 6 m s⁻².

questions.q: A 10 kg mass hangs at rest from a rope. Taking g = 10 m s⁻², what is the tension in the rope?
questions.explanation: At rest, T = mg = 10 × 10 = 100 N.

questions.q: A 500 kg lift is pulled upward by a cable and accelerates upward at 1 m s⁻². Taking g = 10 m s⁻², what is the tension in the cable?
A block just slides down a rough incline of 37° at constant speed. What is the coefficient of kinetic friction? (tan 37° = 0.75.)
questions.explanation: At constant speed mg sinθ = μ mg cosθ, so μ = tan 37° = 0.75.

questions.q: A 0.2 kg ball strikes a wall at 10 m s⁻¹ and rebounds along the same line at 10 m s⁻¹. Find the magnitude of the impulse given to the ball.
questions.explanation: The velocity reverses, so the change in velocity is twice the speed.

questions.q: Masses of 1 kg and 2 kg hang from the ends of a light string over a smooth pulley (g = 10 m s⁻²). Find the acceleration of the masses and the tension in the string.
questions.explanation: Apply Newton's second law to each mass; T = 2m₁m₂g/(m₁ + m₂) = 40/3 N.

questions.q: Power is defined as
questions.explanation: P = W/t.

questions.q: The energy possessed by a body because of its motion is called
questions.explanation: That is the definition of kinetic energy, ½mv².

questions.q: A 3 kg body falls freely from a height of 5 m (g = 10 m s⁻²). What is its kinetic energy just before it reaches the ground?
questions.explanation: KE = loss of PE = mgh = 3 × 10 × 5 = 150 J.

questions.q: A spring of force constant 100 N m⁻¹ is stretched from its natural length by 0.2 m. How much work is done in stretching it?
A 0.1 kg ball hits a wall perpendicularly at 10 m s⁻¹ and bounces back elastically with the same speed. What is the magnitude of the change in its momentum?
questions.explanation: Δp = 0.1 × 10 − (−0.1 × 10) = 2 kg m s⁻¹, even though the kinetic energy does not change.

questions.q: A motor that is 80% efficient does 6000 J of useful work in 10 s. What power does it draw from the supply?
questions.explanation: Useful power = 600 W; input power = 600/0.8 = 750 W.

questions.q: The brakes bring a 1000 kg car moving at 20 m s⁻¹ to rest. Find the work done by the brakes.
questions.answer: −2 × 10⁵ J (the brakes remove 2 × 10⁵ J of kinetic energy)
questions.explanation: By the work–energy theorem the net work equals the change in kinetic energy.

questions.q: A 2 kg block moving at 3 m s⁻¹ collides head-on and elastically with a 1 kg block at rest. Find the velocities of both blocks after the collision.
questions.answer: The 2 kg block moves at 1 m s⁻¹ and the 1 kg block at 4 m s⁻¹, both in the original direction.
keyPoints: Check: momentum 6 = 2 × 1 + 1 × 4; energy 9 J = 1 J + 8 J
questions.explanation: Both momentum and kinetic energy are conserved in an elastic collision.

questions.topic: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.q: What is the SI unit of angular velocity?
questions.explanation: Angular velocity is the angle turned per unit time, in rad s⁻¹.

questions.topic: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.q: A flywheel is fitted to an engine because
options: it reduces the mass of the engine
its large moment of inertia resists sudden changes in rotational speed
questions.explanation: The large moment of inertia keeps the rotation smooth by opposing speed fluctuations.

questions.topic: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.q: Masses of 1 kg, 2 kg and 3 kg are placed on the x-axis at x = 0, 1 m and 2 m. Where is the centre of mass?

questions.topic: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.q: A body has moment of inertia 2 kg m² and an angular acceleration of 3 rad s⁻². What torque acts on it?

questions.topic: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.q: A ring and a disc have the same mass and radius. What is the ratio of the moment of inertia of the ring to that of the disc about the axis through the centre perpendicular to the plane?
questions.explanation: I_ring = MR² and I_disc = ½MR², giving a ratio 2 : 1.

questions.topic: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.q: A uniform metre stick is balanced on a knife edge at the 50 cm mark. A 100 g mass hangs at the 20 cm mark. What mass must hang at the 80 cm mark to keep it balanced?
questions.explanation: Both masses are 30 cm from the pivot, so their torques balance only if the masses are equal.

questions.topic: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.q: A thin ring of mass 2 kg and radius 0.3 m is to be given an angular acceleration of 5 rad s⁻² about its central axis. Find its moment of inertia and the torque required.
questions.answer: I = 0.18 kg m²; torque = 0.9 N m.
questions.explanation: For a ring all the mass is at distance R from the axis.

questions.q: The orbital speed of a satellite in a circular orbit depends on
options: the mass of the planet and the orbital radius
questions.explanation: v = √(GM/r) depends on the planet's mass M and the orbital radius r, not on the satellite's mass.

questions.q: According to Kepler's first law, the orbit of a planet is
options: a circle with the Sun at the centre
an ellipse with the Sun at the centre
an ellipse with the Sun at one focus
questions.explanation: Planets move in elliptical orbits with the Sun at one of the foci.

questions.q: At which place on the Earth's surface is the acceleration due to gravity the largest?
questions.explanation: The Earth is slightly flattened and rotates, so g is greatest at the poles and least at the equator.

questions.q: A 10 kg body is taken to a planet where the acceleration due to gravity is 2.5 m s⁻². What is its weight there?
Two satellites A and B orbit the same planet in circular orbits of radii r and 2r. What is the ratio of their orbital speeds v_A : v_B?
How does the escape speed from the Earth's surface change if the mass of the projectile is doubled?
questions.explanation: v_e = √(2GM/R) does not depend on the mass of the projectile.

questions.q: A planet orbits the Sun at 4 times the Earth's distance from the Sun. Using Kepler's third law, find its orbital period in years.
keyPoints: T² = 4³ = 64 (in years² when r is in astronomical units)
questions.explanation: With T in years and r in Earth–Sun distances, T² = r³.

questions.q: What is the SI unit of stress?
questions.explanation: Stress is force per unit area, measured in N m⁻² or pascal.

questions.q: The shear modulus describes how a solid responds to a deforming force that tends to change its
questions.explanation: Shear stress changes the shape of a body without changing its volume.

questions.q: A 20 kg mass hangs from a wire of cross-section 1 mm². Taking g = 10 m s⁻², what is the tensile stress in the wire?
questions.explanation: Stress = 200 N / 10⁻⁶ m² = 2 × 10⁸ Pa.

questions.q: A material has a bulk modulus of 5 × 10⁹ Pa. What is its compressibility (the reciprocal of the bulk modulus)?
questions.explanation: Compressibility = 1/B = 1/(5 × 10⁹) = 2 × 10⁻¹⁰ Pa⁻¹.

questions.q: A load of 100 N produces an extension of 1 mm in a wire (within the elastic limit). How much elastic potential energy is stored in the wire?
A wire of length L and radius r stretches by x under a load F. A wire of the same material with length 2L and radius 2r carries the same load. What is its extension?
questions.explanation: Extension ∝ L/r², so the factor is 2/4 = 1/2, giving x/2.

questions.q: A steel wire 2 m long and 1 mm in diameter carries a 10 kg load (g = 10 m s⁻²). Young's modulus of steel is 2 × 10¹¹ Pa. Find the extension.
questions.explanation: Extension is FL/(AY) with the cross-sectional area found from the diameter.

questions.q: The property of a fluid by which it resists the relative motion between its layers is called
questions.explanation: Viscosity is the internal friction of a fluid.

questions.q: The angle of contact between pure water and clean glass is
questions.explanation: Water wets glass, so the angle of contact is small and acute.

questions.q: A mercury barometer reads 76 cm. Taking the density of mercury as 13600 kg m⁻³ and g = 9.8 m s⁻², what is the atmospheric pressure?

A soap film is stretched on a wire frame, and a 5 cm long wire slides on it. If the surface tension is 0.03 N m⁻¹ and the film has two surfaces, what force must be applied to the wire to hold it in equilibrium?
Air flows over the top surface of an aircraft wing at 50 m s⁻¹ and under it at 40 m s⁻¹. Taking the density of air as 1.2 kg m⁻³, what is the pressure difference between the lower and upper surfaces?
A piece of ice floats in a glass of water, completely filling it to the brim. When the ice melts, the water level
questions.explanation: The ice displaces a volume of water equal to its own weight; the melted water occupies exactly that volume.

questions.q: Taking atmospheric pressure as 1 × 10⁵ Pa, g = 10 m s⁻² and the density of water as 1000 kg m⁻³, what is the maximum height to which water can be raised by a suction pump?
keyPoints: Maximum height is set by atmospheric pressure: P₀ = ρgh
questions.explanation: Atmospheric pressure can support a water column of about 10 m.

questions.q: In a horizontal pipe, the cross-section narrows from 10 cm² to 5 cm². The pressure in the wide part is 1500 Pa higher than in the narrow part. Using the density of water 1000 kg m⁻³, find the flow speed in the wide part.
questions.answer: 1 m s⁻¹ (and 2 m s⁻¹ in the narrow part)
questions.explanation: Combining continuity and Bernoulli's equation gives the speeds.

questions.q: The boiling point of water at normal atmospheric pressure on the Kelvin scale is about
What is the SI unit of specific latent heat?
questions.explanation: Latent heat per unit mass is L = Q/m, with unit J kg⁻¹.

questions.q: The specific heat of copper is 400 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹. How much heat is needed to raise the temperature of 0.5 kg of copper by 20 K?
A 2 m long rod has a coefficient of linear expansion of 2 × 10⁻⁵ K⁻¹. By how much does its length increase when its temperature rises by 100 K?
A black sphere of radius 0.1 m is at 1000 K. Taking σ = 5.67 × 10⁻⁸ W m⁻² K⁻⁴, approximately how much power does it radiate (treat it as a perfect black body)?
A thin metal plate with a circular hole in it is heated uniformly. What happens to the diameter of the hole?
questions.explanation: The hole expands as if it were made of the same metal, so its diameter increases.

questions.q: How much heat is released when 10 g of steam at 100 °C condenses to water at 100 °C? (Latent heat of vaporisation = 540 cal g⁻¹.)
questions.explanation: Condensation releases the same latent heat that vaporisation absorbs.

questions.q: Which of the following is a state variable (a quantity that depends only on the state of the system)?
questions.explanation: Internal energy depends only on the state of the system; heat and work depend on the process.

questions.q: Which of the following is forbidden by the second law of thermodynamics?
options: Heat flowing from a hot body to a cold body
A cyclic engine converting all the heat from a single reservoir into work
Work being converted completely into heat
A gas expanding into a vacuum
questions.explanation: The Kelvin–Planck statement rules out a cyclic engine with 100% conversion of heat to work.

questions.q: An ideal gas is compressed isothermally. What happens to the heat?
options: The gas gives out heat equal to the work done on it
The gas absorbs heat from the surroundings
The internal energy of the gas increases
questions.explanation: ΔU = 0 for an isothermal process, so Q = W; since W is negative (work done on the gas), Q is negative: heat is released.

questions.q: 2 mol of an ideal gas with Cv = 12.5 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ is heated at constant volume through 10 K. How much heat is absorbed?
questions.explanation: Q = nCvΔT = 2 × 12.5 × 10 = 250 J (no work is done at constant volume).

questions.q: A refrigerator has a coefficient of performance of 5. How much work is needed to remove 1000 J of heat from the cold space?
questions.explanation: COP = Q_cold/W, so W = 1000/5 = 200 J.

questions.q: On a P–V diagram, an adiabatic curve through a point compared with the isothermal curve through the same point is
questions.explanation: For an adiabatic process PV^γ = constant with γ > 1, so the curve falls more steeply than an isotherm.

questions.q: A gas absorbs 400 J of heat and does 150 J of work. Find the change in its internal energy.
questions.explanation: The heat not converted into work raises the internal energy.

questions.q: The ideal gas equation for n moles of a gas is
questions.explanation: PV = nRT relates pressure, volume, temperature and amount of gas.

questions.q: The Boltzmann constant has a value of about
questions.explanation: k_B = R/N_A ≈ 1.38 × 10⁻²³ J K⁻¹.

questions.q: What is the density of oxygen gas (molar mass 32 g mol⁻¹) at STP? (Molar volume = 22.4 L.)
questions.explanation: Density = 32 g / 22.4 L ≈ 1.43 g L⁻¹ = 1.43 kg m⁻³.

questions.q: The average translational kinetic energy per molecule of a gas at 600 K compared with that at 300 K is
questions.explanation: Average KE = (3/2)k_BT is proportional to T, so it doubles.

questions.q: What is the molar specific heat at constant volume of a monatomic ideal gas? (R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹.)
Helium (molar mass 4 g mol⁻¹) and hydrogen (H₂, molar mass 2 g mol⁻¹) are at the same temperature. What is the ratio of the rms speed of helium molecules to that of hydrogen molecules?
questions.explanation: v_rms ∝ 1/√M, so the ratio is √(2/4) = 1/√2.

questions.q: How many moles of a gas are there in 3.011 × 10²³ molecules? (N_A = 6.022 × 10²³ mol⁻¹.)
questions.explanation: Divide the number of molecules by Avogadro's number.

questions.q: A source vibrates at a frequency of 50 Hz. What is its time period?
When the frequency of an external periodic force equals the natural frequency of an oscillator, the amplitude of oscillation becomes
questions.explanation: This is resonance.

questions.q: A mass on a spring of force constant 40π² N m⁻¹ has a time period of 1 s. What is the mass?
questions.explanation: T² = 4π²m/k, so m = kT²/(4π²) = 40π²/(4π²) = 10 kg.

questions.q: A particle in SHM has displacement x = A cos ωt. At t = 0 which of the following is true?
questions.explanation: At t = 0 the particle is at the extreme position x = A, where speed and KE are zero and PE is maximum.

questions.q: A particle performs SHM with a time period of 4 s and amplitude 8 cm, starting from the mean position. How long does it take to reach a displacement of 4 cm?
questions.explanation: x = A sin ωt gives sin ωt = 0.5, so ωt = π/6 and t = T/12 = 1/3 s.

questions.q: A simple pendulum is suspended in a lift that accelerates upward. Compared with the lift at rest, its time period
questions.explanation: The effective gravity becomes g + a, which is larger, so T = 2π√(l/g_eff) decreases.

questions.q: A 2 kg mass attached to a spring oscillates with a time period of 0.628 s. Find the force constant of the spring.
questions.explanation: Rearranging T = 2π√(m/k) gives k = 4π²m/T².

questions.q: A travelling wave transports
questions.explanation: Waves carry energy and momentum from place to place without bulk transport of the medium.

questions.q: Ultrasonic waves are sound waves with frequencies
questions.explanation: Ultrasound lies above the audible range, i.e. above about 20 kHz.

questions.q: A wave is given by y = 0.1 sin(4πt − 2πx) in SI units. What is its frequency?
questions.explanation: ω = 4π rad s⁻¹, so f = ω/2π = 2 Hz.

questions.q: A string 1 m long is fixed at both ends and the wave speed on it is 200 m s⁻¹. What is its fundamental frequency?
An open organ pipe and a closed organ pipe have the same length. How does the fundamental frequency of the open pipe compare with that of the closed pipe?
options: It is four times as large
questions.explanation: Open pipe: f = v/2L; closed pipe: f = v/4L, so the open pipe's frequency is double.

questions.q: A source emits a note of 340 Hz. An observer moves towards the stationary source at 17 m s⁻¹. If the speed of sound is 340 m s⁻¹, what frequency does the observer hear?
A wave on a string has a frequency of 50 Hz and a wavelength of 0.4 m. Find its speed and the time it takes to travel 10 m along the string.
questions.explanation: Use v = fλ, then time = distance/speed.
